body.rendered:
# Migration plan: demo-plan

## Overview
Data moves from node f4921c57-7924-43bd-b50c-709a68314471 to node 2a18da67-fe92-4774-a4e2-b8ae1cb0585b.
The backup is kept on the source server: a full snapshot first, then a delta shortly before cutover.
Transport: 49dc115f-994f-42d1-b4d0-85984e62742e; encryption: encrypted on your side before upload.
Cutover by tunnel. DNS snapshot first: yes. Rollback available: yes.
Databases listed: 0 (0 restored, 0 copied under a suffixed name, 0 skipped).
Data that already exists on the target is never overwritten; it is kept and the incoming copy gets a suffixed name.

## Steps, in the order they run
1. Collect an inventory - source server (risk: Read)
Impact: Reads what runs on the machine; changes nothing.
Runs first; it depends on nothing.
2. Collect an inventory - target server (risk: Read)
Impact: Reads what runs on the machine; changes nothing.
Runs first; it depends on nothing.
3. Take the backup (risk: Light change)
Impact: Creates a snapshot of the data; the running services keep running and use extra disk and CPU.
Runs after step 1, 2.
4. Move the backup to the target (risk: Light change)
Impact: Copies the snapshot over the chosen transport; uses network bandwidth; the source is untouched.
Runs after step 3.
5. Restore on the target (risk: Risky change)
Impact: Writes data on the target. Existing data there is not overwritten.
Runs after step 4.
It can only be approved in the panel, not from a chat bot.
6. Verify the target (risk: Read)
Impact: Checks that the target runs and matches the source; changes nothing.
Runs after step 5.
7. Copy what changed since the snapshot (risk: Risky change)
Impact: Brings the target up to date shortly before cutover; writes data on the target.
Runs after step 6.
It can only be approved in the panel, not from a chat bot.
8. Move traffic to the target (risk: Risky change)
Impact: Visitors start reaching the target. This is the moment the migration becomes visible.
Runs after step 7.
It can only be approved in the panel, not from a chat bot.
9. Verify again after cutover (risk: Read)
Impact: Checks the target under real traffic; changes nothing.
Runs after step 8.
10. Shut down the old server (risk: Destructive)
Impact: Destroys the old server as a fallback. It cannot be undone.
Runs after step 9.
You must type the name of the server to confirm; it can only be approved in the panel.

## Where you can stop
Until the cutover step, the old server keeps serving and nothing visible has changed: you can stop at any step and nothing needs undoing on the source.
At the cutover step traffic moves. Rollback available: yes. After it, going back means using the rollback.
Shutting down the old server is the point of no return. Do not approve it before the conditions below are met.

## What the time depends on
The amount of data to copy (this plan does not measure it).
The speed of the connection between the machines and the storage.
The number of databases to restore (0 listed).
The size of the changes made after the snapshot (the delta).

## Before the old server may be shut down
The old server may be shut down only when every condition below is met:
- No critical finding is open: met
- The inventories behind the comparison are complete: not met
- The target was verified again after traffic moved: checked when the plan runs

## Left out of the backup
These are left out of the backup because they can be rebuilt. Check that nothing you need is on this list:
- logs: log files
- cache: cache directories
- node_modules: node_modules (reinstalled from the lock file)
- tmp: temporary files
- pycache: compiled Python caches

## Findings that block
No critical finding is open.
An inventory behind the findings is incomplete (or the target was not collected), so an empty list is not proof. Collect again before the cutover.
